title: MDX slide deck
description: Turns the app into a slide deck written in slides.mdx: top-level --- separates slides, layouts, reveal steps, speaker notes, shadcn/ui components sized for slides and Motion need no import, <Include> pulls in slides from other files, and <Slide hidden> drafts show only on the dev server. The deck scales its canvas to any screen with Motion transitions, an overview, a go-to palette, a presenter view kept in sync across windows, clicks on a slide shared between those windows, and a print view for PDF, a page per slide or per step; every slide reports content that does not fit. Slide and step live in the URL, so a reload or a hot update keeps the place.

context_before: # Written by the shadcn CLI; left as generated so re-adding one shows real changes.
added: # Prettier moves text inside JSX onto lines of its own, which MDX then reads
# as a paragraph: formatting would change how the slides render.
Slides written in MDX and rendered with React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui and Motion. The deck is `slides.mdx`; `pnpm dev` shows it, and every save updates the slide you are on.

removed: | `pnpm dev`       | Serves the app with hot reload                    |
added: | `pnpm dev`       | Serves the deck with hot reload                   |
context_after: | `pnpm build`     | Type-checks and builds a static site into `dist/` |

context_before: UI components come from [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com): `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>` adds one under `src/components/ui`, themed by the tokens in `src/index.css`.
added: `---` on its own line, with a blank line before it, starts a new slide. The YAML frontmatter at the top configures the deck:
| `title`        | first slide's heading | Browser tab and presenter title                   |
| `width`        | `960`                 | Canvas width in CSS pixels, scaled to fit         |
Everything in `src/mdx-components.tsx` is available without an import:
| `<Slide className transition>`                          | Wrap a slide's content to style it or give it its own transition                  |
| `<Slide hidden>`                                        | A draft: shown by the dev server, left out of the build                           |
| `<Cover>`, `<Section>`, `<Statement>`, `<Quote author>` | Layouts that fill the slide; `variant="primary"` fills it with the primary colour |
| `<Columns>`                                             | Side-by-side columns, split at `---` inside it                                    |
| `<Steps dim>`                                           | Reveals list items, or children, one step at a time                               |
| `<Step>`                                                | Reveals its content on the next step                                              |
| `<Notes>`                                               | Speaker notes, shown only in the presenter view                                   |
| `<Callout title variant>`                               | An alert sized for slides                                                         |
| `<Stat value label>`                                    | One number, large, with what it counts; compare several in `<Columns>`            |
| `<Include src="./chapters/intro.mdx" />`                | The slides of another file, in its place                                          |

Text inside a JSX element stays inline when it is on the same line as the tags; put blank lines around Markdown that should become paragraphs. Import anything else at the top of the deck (`import { Rocket } from "lucide-react"`), and put images in `public/` and reference them without a leading slash (`![Diagram](images/diagram.png)`) so the build works under any path.
A long talk can be split into files: an included file is a list of slides like the deck itself, with imports relative to it, and editing it updates the deck.

To make a component of your own advance with the deck, reserve steps on the slide: `const { ref, step } = useSteps(3)` from `src/deck/steps.tsx` gives the element behind `ref` three steps and tells it how many have been reached.
While `pnpm dev` runs, a slide whose content does not fit says so in its top corner, in red, and content shrunk to fit says so in amber.
| <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd> <kbd>PgDn</kbd> | Next step (a presentation clicker sends Page Down)      |
| <kbd>⇧</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> / <kbd>←</kbd>      | Next or previous slide, skipping steps                  |
| <kbd>G</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd>     | Go to a slide by number or title                        |
| <kbd>P</kbd>                                  | Presenter view: notes, next slide, timer, in its window |

The URL holds the slide and step (`#/4/2`), so a reload keeps your place, and the audience and presenter windows follow each other. So do clicks on a slide: a fold or a tab picked by hand holds until the next step, and a diff's view or a folder until the next slide. The print button in the toolbar opens `#/print`: every slide fully revealed, one per page, ready for the browser's Save as PDF with background graphics on. `#/print/steps` prints a page per step instead.
`pnpm build` writes a static site with relative paths: `dist/` can be served from any host or sub-path.

`src/index.css` holds the shadcn/ui colour tokens for light and dark mode, the fonts and the radius; the slides, the controls and the code frames all follow it. Paste a theme from [tweakcn](https://tweakcn.com) or the [shadcn/ui themes](https://ui.shadcn.com/themes) over the `:root` and `.dark` blocks to restyle everything.

For a brand, set `--primary` to its colour and `--primary-foreground` to the text that goes on it, in both blocks, and `--foreground` if the brand has a text colour. Put its logo files in `public/`, and give the cover, section and closing slides `variant="primary"`: they fill with the brand colour, and the highlight in code, the numbers of `<Stat>` and the cover's glow follow it. White text on a saturated brand colour is often close to the 4.5:1 contrast body text needs, so keep text on it large.

<small className="text-lg text-muted-foreground">Press <Kbd>→</Kbd> to begin and <Kbd>?</Kbd> for every shortcut.</small>
## Slides are Markdown and JSX, split at `---`
`slides.mdx` is the deck, and every save updates the slide on screen. The
frontmatter at the top configures it.
The frontmatter sets the title, the transition and the colour scheme. Every
slide is a `<Slide>`; write one yourself to give it a `className` or its own
## Steps reveal a list one item at a time
- Each press of <Kbd>→</Kbd> reveals the next item
- `<Steps dim>` fades the items already seen
- Each press reveals the next item
Speaker notes live in `<Notes>`: hidden on the slide, shown in the presenter
view (press **P**). This slide has four steps, so the presenter shows them too.
## Layouts and shadcn/ui components need no import
fill the slide, and anything in `src/mdx-components.tsx` is in scope.
<Callout title="Callouts">An Alert with an icon, sized for slides.</Callout>
`<Columns>` splits its content at `---`. Add your own components to
`src/mdx-components.tsx` to use them on every slide without an import.
## A claim with its evidence beat a title with bullets, in half the words
<Stat value="21" label="words a slide: one claim, visual evidence" />
<Stat value="42" label="words a slide: a topic title and bullets" />
`<Stat>` shows one number with what it counts. Garner and Alley, 2013: 110
engineering students watched the same narrated lesson with one of the two
decks; comprehension was 9.4 against 6.7 out of 15.
## Anything can animate, because `motion` is in scope
Slides transition with Motion, `<Steps>` reveal with it, and
`<Slide transition="zoom">` changes how one slide arrives.
## The presenter view has your notes, the next slide and a timer
- <Kbd>P</Kbd> opens it, and both windows follow each other
- <Kbd>O</Kbd> shows every slide, <Kbd>G</Kbd> finds one by title
- <Kbd>B</Kbd> blacks out the screen, <Kbd>F</Kbd> goes fullscreen
<CardDescription>The print button in the toolbar shows every slide fully revealed, ready to save as a PDF.</CardDescription>
The URL holds the slide and the step, so a reload keeps your place.
## Drafts stay out of the build
`<Slide hidden>` shows the slide on the dev server only, marked in its corner.
Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there
is nothing left to take away.
